sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface trafficking confirmed by live-cell fluorescent anti-Myc antibody staining; quantitative fluorescence microscopy used to assess surface levels of wildtype and variant isoforms. Functional assays beyond surface delivery not reported for this tag position.
sites.rationale: PCDHGC5 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with a signal peptide (residues 1–29) and a single extracellular N-terminus (residues 30–693); the C-terminus is intracellular. Because exactly one extracellular terminus exists, an 'extracellular Myc tag' on a cPCDH construct can only reside at the mature N-terminus, after signal-peptide cleavage. Python confirmed residue 29 (G) is the last signal-peptide residue and residue 30 (Q) is the first mature extracellular residue; insert_after_residue = 29 places the tag at the mature N-terminus, 664 residues from the TM boundary. Evidence is indirect (γC3 ortholog, same γC subfamily, same domain architecture), so position_evidence is topology_derived. PMC12157453 (L2) reports clustered PCDH constructs — including the γC3 isoform, a close ortholog of γC5 in the same γC subfamily — engineered with an extracellular Myc tag and an intracellular fluorescent protein. Surface staining with fluorescent anti-Myc antibodies in transfected cells confirmed surface trafficking of the tagged constructs. No residue number is stated in the clip.

sources.claim: Using cPCDH constructs containing an extracellular Myc tag and an intracellular fluorescent protein (FP; Figure S1A ), we added fluorescent anti-Myc antibodies (Ab) to transfected cells and collected fluorescence microscopy images.

literature_notes: L1 (PMC3209968) reports a C-terminal EGFP fusion on full-length Pcdh-γC5 expressed in HEK293 cells, confirmed by anti-Pcdh-γC5 immunofluorescence. The C-terminus (residue 944) falls entirely within the intracellular domain (715–944); this tag is therefore not a surface tag and is recorded in other_positions. L2 (PMC12157453) is the sole ledger line supporting an extracellular tag; it names γC3 explicitly and cPCDH constructs generally, making it indirect evidence for γC5. No residue number is given, but topology_derived reasoning yields a unique junction (after residue 29). No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for PCDHGC5 or a close ortholog.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal EGFP fused to full-length Pcdh-γC5 and expressed in HEK293 cells; the C-terminus (residue 944) lies in the intracellular domain (715–944), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface epitope site.
